title: Canonical finite-field coefficient module diagram and closure cocone
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with the finite-subextension-valued condensed convention [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], $E\subseteq\Omega$ a finite intermediate field, and $X$ a scheme. Use the reconstructed section-ring module categories and their fixed termwise section-action equivalence [def-sfb-internal-section-total-comparison]. Let $I_E=\operatorname{AsSmall}(E\downarrow\mathrm{FinInt}(\Omega))$ in coefficient universe $u+1$, and let $H_E:I_E\to\mathrm{FinInt}(\Omega)$ be the inverse small-equivalence followed by the forgetful functor. For the regular $E_X$-module in degree zero, take the canonical scalar-inclusion complex diagram and its specified closure cocone [def-weil-pbc-condensed-coefficient-complex-diagram], with both structure inclusions $E\subseteq H_E(i)$ given by the object of the under-category. Define the coefficient module diagram by applying the fixed termwise section-action equivalence and evaluating at degree zero. Define its coefficient cocone by applying the same functors to that specified complex cocone. Thus its stage is the scalar extension of the regular $E_X$-module to $H_E(i)_X$, restricted back to $E_X$ and transported to section modules; its vertex is the analogous extension to $\Omega_X$. Its transitions and legs are the actual scalar-inclusion maps supplied by that complex diagram and cocone. This defines the index projection, module diagram and cocone only, and asserts no colimit, freeness or flatness property.
